name: American Red Cross
summary: US disaster relief, home fire safety, services to military families, international relief and preparedness, and household visits for measles campaigns; it also supplies about 40% of the US blood supply and runs CPR and first-aid training, both paid for by hospitals and course fees.

programs.label: Disaster relief, home fire safety, military families and community services (US)
programs.weight_source: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/about-us/publications/2025-publications/2025-Consolidated-Financial-Statement.pdf (FY2025, p. 4): Domestic Disaster Services $625,411k + Services to the Armed Forces $80,621k + Community Services $14,977k. Weights are the spending donations pay for: these programmes earn no fees.

programs.label: Measles & Rubella Partnership household visits
programs.weight_source: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/about-us/publications/2025-publications/2025-Consolidated-Financial-Statement.pdf (FY2025, p. 4): International Relief and Development Services $48,839k, funded by donations, times the Measles & Rubella Partnership's share (@american_red_cross.msl_spend_share, best 0.08: measles and rubella grants were $1,655,057 of $21,634,748 in grants abroad, Form 990 Schedule F) = $3,907.1k. The rest of the international programme is the relief-abroad programme.

programs.label: Disaster relief and preparedness abroad (grants to Red Cross and Red Crescent societies)
programs.weight_source: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/about-us/publications/2025-publications/2025-Consolidated-Financial-Statement.pdf (FY2025, p. 4): International Relief and Development Services $48,839k, funded by donations, times one minus the Measles & Rubella Partnership's share (@american_red_cross.msl_spend_share, best 0.08) = $44,931.9k.

programs.label: Blood supply and lifesaving training (paid for by hospitals and course fees)
programs.weight_source: https://www.redcross.org/content/dam/redcross/about-us/publications/2025-publications/2025-Consolidated-Financial-Statement.pdf (FY2025, p. 4): Biomedical Services cost $2,119,409k against $2,305,215k of biomedical revenue from hospitals, and Training Services $143,102k against $175,385k of programme-materials (course) revenue. Fees cover both in full, so no donated dollar funds them: weight 0 (only donated money's share counts).
